findings.title: Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws a TypeError
findings.description: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` produces `undefined` when there is no destination calendar. Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which fell back to Cal Video. `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` produces `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination, so this state is reachable. `EventManager.create` is called at `handleNewBooking.ts:2114` in an `else if` branch outside any try block, so the booking request fails with a 500. The repo does not enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, so TypeScript will not flag it. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Google update and delete fallback lookup can never match
findings.description: The fallback runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares `externalId` against a falsy value. `DestinationCalendar.externalId` is a non-null string, so the lookup always returns `undefined`. The same expression appears at lines 315-317 in `deleteEvent`. The old fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result, `updateEvent` passes `calendarId: undefined` and fails, and `deleteEvent` falls through to `"primary"`. A 404 is resolved silently, so the event stays on the real destination calendar. This affects every reference stored without an `externalCalendarId`, which the `create` path now produces for credential-less destinations (next finding). Fix: fall back to the matched destination's externalId, not a comparison against the falsy input.

findings.title: Google insert routes credential-less destinations to primary and leaves the patch unguarded
findings.description: Only a destination whose `credentialId` equals the calling credential's id is matched. Credential-less destinations never match, so the insert goes to `primary` (line 154) even though a destination is configured. The old code used `destinationCalendar.externalId`. The code still handles credential-less destinations (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:375-382` calls `createEvent(c, event)` without an externalId), so such rows must still exist. The reference they produce has no `externalCalendarId`. The organizer attendee email (lines 122-124) still uses the destination's externalId, so the event can sit on `primary` while the email points at another calendar. Line 168 also passes `selectedCalendar` as `calendarId` to `events.patch` for the Meet hangout link. That call has no callback and no catch, and `selectedCalendar` can now be undefined, so the patch can reject with nothing listening. Fix: compute the calendar id once, with a fallback to the matched destination, and reuse it for the insert, the patch, and the organizer email.

findings.title: Office365, Lark, and CalDAV adapters ignore the per-credential destination
findings.description:
These three `createEvent` implementations read `event.destinationCalendar[0]` regardless of which credential is calling. `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now passes the full destination list to every credential, including COLLECTIVE team members. Consequences:
- Office365 (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-77`) and Lark (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-129`) post to the first destination's calendar ID using the member's token. The request fails.
- CalDAV (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-165`) filters the credential's calendars to those matching `[0]`. A member's CalDAV account usually has none, so nothing is written. The method still returns a success object (lines 185-191), so the event is silently dropped.

The Google adapter was fixed to match by `credentialId`, but these three were not. Fix: select the destination for the current credential in each adapter, using the externalId that `CalendarManager.createEvent` already receives.

findings.title: Organization slug condition inverted
findings.description: The original spread was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which stores the slug when billing is disabled. The diff changes it to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which stores the slug only when billing is enabled. With billing disabled, new organizations get no slug. `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getPublicEvent.ts:163` and `:242` treat a null organization slug as unpublished, so those organizations would be hidden. This edit has nothing to do with destination calendars and the diff gives no reason for it. Revert it, or justify the change in its own PR.

findings.title: loadUsers catch exposes raw Prisma errors and swallows the rest without logging
findings.description: The new `try/catch` around `loadUsers` does two things. `HttpError` and `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` are rethrown as 400 with the raw `error.message`, which can expose database details to the booker. Any other error, including a database outage, becomes a generic 500 and the original error is never logged. The previous code did not catch these errors at all. Also, `if (!Array.isArray(hosts))` at line 746 is dead code, because `hosts` is `eventType.hosts || []`. Fix: log the original error, and return a generic message rather than the Prisma text.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none
findings.description: When both the event type and the organizer lack a destination calendar, `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` (lines 1063-1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` at line 1078 is then a no-op, so no team member's calendar receives the event. Team destinations are also collected as a side effect inside the `users.slice(1).map(...)` callback (lines 990-994), which pushes into an outer array while building the attendee list. Fix: start from `[]`, always push, and collect the team destinations in a plain loop.

findings.title: Booking webhook payload changes shape and gains an unused field
findings.description: `webhookData` spreads `evt` (`...evt`), so outgoing booking webhook payloads now send `destinationCalendar` as an array where they used to send an object. They also now include `schedulingType`, which was added at line 1074. Nothing reads `schedulingType` from a `CalendarEvent`, so it only widens the payload. Consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e expectations are also inconsistent: `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249` now expects `[]`, while lines 119 and 373 still expect `null` for the same field. Fix: keep the public payload shape, or document the change, and remove `schedulingType` if nothing consumes it.

findings.title: Duplicated credential-loading and destination-wrapping logic
findings.description: The same 25-line block that loads a credential from the database and maps it to the credential shape is copied into `createAllCalendarEvents` (lines 341-368) and `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 515-541). `handleCancelBooking.ts:431-441` has a third variant. The `x ? [x] : []` wrapping for destinations is repeated at about ten call sites: `handleCancelBooking.ts:251` and `:528`, `confirm.handler.ts:175`, `editLocation.handler.ts:85`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts:240`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts:290`, `paypal-webhook.ts:152`, `ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:101` and `:207`, and `handleNewBooking.ts:1063`. Extract one helper for credential loading and one for destination wrapping.

findings.title: Cancel flow repeats the recurring-delete block once per calendar reference
findings.description: The `_calendar` references are now iterated in a loop. The recurring-cancel block (lines 445-468) does not depend on the current reference. It loops over all user calendar credentials and all `updatedBookings`, so with N calendar references it runs N times and pushes duplicate delete promises into `apiDeletes`. The same change fans out in `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:504-550`). Each reference with no `credentialId` now updates every credential of its type, where previously only the first reference was used. Fix: move the recurring-delete block out of the loop so it runs once.

findings.title: No tests cover the rewritten destination routing
findings.description: No test file in this tree references `destinationCalendar`, `createAllCalendarEvents`, or `updateAllCalendarEvents`. The diff rewrites the multi-destination routing in `EventManager`, all four calendar adapters, the cancel and reschedule flows, and the Google update and delete lookup, but adds no unit tests for any of them. The only test change is one payload expectation in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`, which is inconsistent with the other `null` expectations in the same file. Tests for the Meet-without-destination case, credential-less destinations, COLLECTIVE events with mixed credential types, and updates or deletes with a null `externalCalendarId` would have caught the FAIL findings above.

findings.title: Credential fallback loads any credential by id without an ownership check
findings.description: When a credential is not on the booking owner's list, the code loads it by id from the database and uses it to delete or update events. The same pattern appears at `packages/core/EventManager.ts:515-523`. The ids come from booking references and destinations, which the server writes, so the exposure is limited. The code still does not confirm that the credential belongs to the booking's host or team. Consider checking the credential's `userId` or `teamId` against the event's hosts and members.

findings.title: `isTeamEventType` drops enum typing and mixes styles
findings.description: `isTeamEventType` was rewritten from `SchedulingType` enum comparisons to an untyped string array. `["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(...)` loses enum checking, and the `!!` guard is redundant. The file now uses `SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` at line 805 and `"COLLECTIVE"` literals at lines 992 and 1077. Use the enum consistently.

findings.title: Unrelated user-visible text change
findings.description: The calendar-notes text changes from "organiser" to "organizer". The change is user-visible and unrelated to this PR. Split it out, or call it out in the PR description.

findings.title: Destination update path leaves a stale credentialId
findings.description: The destination update path sets `integration` and `externalId` but leaves `credentialId` unchanged. If the destination moves to a calendar on a different credential, the stored `credentialId` no longer matches. The new credential-based matching in the Google adapter (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-149`) would then route events to `primary`. This predates the diff, but the change makes it matter. Set `credentialId` in this update as well.
